body:
## Problem

The Insert-session (`Insstart`) is not scoped to a buffer/window, and plugins can't know when it changes. A plugin might be building an insert-session, but `Insstart` gets reset if curbuf changes *and* keys execute. Then the plugin is confused. There is no error, no event, no way to detect it.

Use-case: vscode-neovim wants to "record text as the last insert, so `.` repeats it", without hijacking the live session. Currently(?) the only way to express that is to type into a scratch buffer.

### Repro steps

RPC client (such as [vscode-neovim](https://github.com/vscode-neovim/vscode-neovim)) making API calls:

1. `nvim_input('i')` in `blah blah` with the cursor at column 5 — session starts there.
2. `nvim_buf_set_text()` inserts `blah blah` at column 5; `nvim_win_set_cursor()` moves the cursor to column 14. (This is how a UI that owns editing applies typed text.)
3. Open a scratch window, `nvim_feedkeys('blah blah', 'n', true)` into it, close it, return to the original window. Mode is still `i`, cursor still `[1, 14]`.
4. `nvim_input('<C-u>')`.

| | result |
|---|---|
| v0.12.5 | `"blah blah"` — deletes the entered text |
| master  | `"blah"` — deletes to the line start |

Scoping the buffer instead of switching windows does not help, because the session is global:

```lua
vim._with({ buf = tmp }, function()
  vim.api.nvim_feedkeys('iblah blah', 'nx', false)  -- 'x' flushes inside the scope
end)
-- text lands in `tmp`, but the caller's session is gone; CTRL-U now deletes the line
```

Bisected to 2445fab6fb8c: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2445fab6fb8c9b4d372ba7c02ff9fd1a2db6e4a4/src/nvim/edit.c#L2210-L2211


The patch correctly avoids a stale `Insstart` after an external cursor move. But clients such as vscode-neovim may accidentally depend on that staleness.



## Ideas(?)

1. 🤔 (recommended) Let `nvim_buf_set_text` update dot-repeat. #19806
2. 🤔 Let plugins set dot-repeat: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41387
3. 😕 (over-specific?) Expose `Insstart` as `v:insstart`. Or maybe via `nvim_get_mode()`.
4. 😕 (over-specific?) Emit an event when the Insert-session is re-anchored or dropped by something other than user typing (API edit, `<Cmd>` cursor move, keys fed to another buffer).
5. 😕 (?) Make the `i_CTRL-U` fallback non-destructive by default

### Notes

- vscode-neovim workaround: https://github.com/vscode-neovim/vscode-neovim/pull/2637
- Note this is not solved by a synchronous primitive: `nvim_feedkeys(..., 'x')` already executes until typeahead is empty, and `vim._with({ buf = … })` already scopes the buffer. Both work as documented, and neither helps, because they scope *where the keys land*, not *which session owns the typing*.

comment_data.body:
I dug into this a bit and reproduced it on `9f425311c3`. I split the scratch-buffer steps into separate functional tests:

- API edit alone: `<C-u>` preserves the original text.
- API edit + opening/closing an empty scratch window: also fine.
- API edit + typing into the scratch window: `<C-u>` leaves `"blah"` instead of `"blah blah"`.

The mode and cursor are the same before `<C-u>` in all three cases, so that seems to isolate the replayed typing rather than the window switch itself.

One history detail worth noting: `13def2fa3a` narrowed the unconditional reset from `2445fab6fb8c`. In the current `stop_arrow()` code, the boundary is only pulled backward when the cursor precedes it. The scratch cursor at column zero still satisfies that comparison, without any buffer identity attached to the position. `Ins.start` then gets copied to `Ins.start_orig`, which the backspace path uses as its stopping point. This code now lives in `src/nvim/insert.c`.

I also tried a small local experiment toward #19806: recording API-applied insertions through the existing paste-recording machinery, without scratch typing. In the cases I tested, that preserved `ciw`, insert counts, undo, and `<C-u>`. That’s consistent with your earlier comment on #19806 about reusing the machinery from #30438.

The experiment is only insertion support, though—not a solution for the full client workflow. In particular:

- Recording `ab`, then deleting `b` through the API, still repeats `ab` unless the deletion is represented too.
- Paste recording alone joins edits across API cursor moves; it doesn’t determine whether they belong to one continuous change.
- Turning a range deletion into a number of `<BS>` keys isn’t necessarily equivalent: with `softtabstop=4`, one backspace can delete four spaces.

So this gives some concrete support for option 1, but I don’t think it settles the API or grouping semantics. Would a standalone functional reproducer be the most useful contribution here, or would a narrowly scoped insertion-recording proof of concept help the discussion around #19806/#30450?

> * Recording `ab`, then deleting `b` through the API, still repeats `ab` unless the deletion is represented too

wdym "recording ab"? concrete example. in less than 30 words please.

> the most useful contribution here

my assumption/hope is `nvim_buf_set_text` can just gain a `opts.undo` parameter. that should buy time and will let us discover what/if more is needed in the long term.

Sorry that was my insertion-only experiment.... inserting “hello” through the API then deleting “o” without recording the deletion, leaves “hell” in the document but repeats “hello”.

I added the `opts.undo` parameter to `nvim_buf_set_text` and so far the API insertions can be repeated without typing into a scratch buffer and so far `ciw`, dot-repeat, undo, Ctrl-U tests are passing.

Deletion and replacement recording aren’t implemented yet which I'm working on now, if I'm not going the right direction let me know.
